bibliographic.title: Foundation metrics for evaluating effectiveness of healthcare conversations powered by generative AI
bibliographic.authors: Mahyar Abbasian, Elahe Khatibi, Iman Azimi, David Oniani, Zahra Shakeri Hossein Abad, Alexander Thieme, Ram Sriram, Zhongqi Yang, Yanshan Wang, Bryant Lin, Olivier Gevaert, Li-Jia Li, Ramesh Jain, Amir M. Rahmani
bibliographic.citation_apa: Abbasian, M., Khatibi, E., Azimi, I., Oniani, D., Shakeri Hossein Abad, Z., Thieme, A., Sriram, R., Yang, Z., Wang, Y., Lin, B., Gevaert, O., Li, L.-J., Jain, R., & Rahmani, A. M. (2024). Foundation metrics for evaluating effectiveness of healthcare conversations powered by generative AI. npj Digital Medicine, 7, 82. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-024-01074-z

methodology.method_family: perspective literature review and framework proposal
methodology.study_design: Perspective article reviewing intrinsic and extrinsic LLM evaluation metrics and proposing healthcare chatbot foundation metrics
methodology.technology_context: Generative AI, large language models, interactive conversational models (chatbots) for healthcare tasks including diagnosis support, education, mental health, scheduling, and triaging

eligibility.decision_rationale: Perspective article focused on proposing and reviewing evaluation metrics for LLM-based healthcare chatbots. Strong alignment with conversational AI, LLMs, and regulated healthcare, and it addresses trust, ethics, bias, and user-centered assessment. Primary contribution is an evaluation-metrics framework rather than operational conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit systems, or human oversight architecture.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was provided; full metric taxonomy, implementation guidance, and governance-related sections may extend beyond the supplied excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal adapted to a non-empirical perspective/framework paper. Literature coverage appears structured by intrinsic versus extrinsic metrics, but systematic search and selection procedures are not evidenced in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The article presents a coherent user-centered metrics framework for healthcare chatbots and explicitly addresses ethics, trust, bias, and robustness. Confidence is moderate because the supplied text does not document a systematic review protocol or empirical validation of the proposed metrics.

coding.theme: Evaluation frameworks for healthcare conversational AI
coding.subtheme: Foundation metrics for LLM-powered healthcare dialogues

synthesis.main_claim: Healthcare applications require a unified, comprehensive set of foundation metrics to evaluate LLM-based conversational models because generic LLM metrics fail to capture medical concepts and user-centered aspects such as trust, ethics, empathy, and personalization.
synthesis.contribution: Reviews state-of-the-art intrinsic and extrinsic LLM evaluation metrics and proposes a comprehensive, user-centered metric set for assessing healthcare chatbots across language processing, clinical task impact, and interactive conversation effectiveness.
synthesis.limitations: The provided text emphasizes challenges in defining and implementing metrics, including target audience, evaluation methods, and prompt techniques; broader governance implementation constraints are only partially evidenced in the excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on how conversational LLM effectiveness, safety, and trust-related dimensions can be operationalized through evaluation metrics in regulated healthcare settings; not primary evidence for operational governance architectures.

evidence.excerpt: npj | digital medicine Perspective Published in partnership with Seoul National University Bundang Hospital https://doi.org/10.1038/s41746-024-01074-z Foundation metrics for evaluating effectiveness of healthcare conversations powered by generative AI

evidence.claim: Study focuses on LLM-based healthcare chatbots and the need for healthcare-specific evaluation metrics.
evidence.excerpt: The purpose of this paper is to explore state-of-the-art LLM-based evaluation metrics that are specifically applicable to the assessment of interactive conversational models in healthcare.

evidence.claim: Regulated, life-critical healthcare context motivates specialized evaluation.
evidence.excerpt: The life-critical nature of healthcare applications necessitates establishing a unified and comprehensive set of evaluation metrics for conversational models.

evidence.claim: Generic LLM metrics neglect user-centered governance-relevant dimensions such as trust and ethics.
evidence.excerpt: Moreover, these metrics neglect pivotal user-centered aspects, including trust-building, ethics, personalization, empathy, user comprehension, and emotional support.

evidence.claim: Paper uses a literature review of intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation methods.
evidence.excerpt: The evaluation of language models can be categorized into intrinsic and extrinsic methods18, which can be executed automatically or manually.

evidence.claim: Intrinsic metrics are inadequate for healthcare chatbots.
evidence.excerpt: However, they solely rely on surface-form similarity and language-specific perspectives, rendering them inadequate for healthcare chatbots.

evidence.claim: Extrinsic metrics incorporate user perspectives and human participation.
evidence.excerpt: Extrinsic evaluation metrics present means of measuring the performance of language models by incorporating user perspectives and real-world contexts18.

evidence.claim: Proposed metrics assess healthcare chatbots from an end-user perspective.
evidence.excerpt: we present a comprehensive set of metrics essential for conducting a user-centered evaluation of LLM-based healthcare chatbots.

evidence.claim: Robustness is framed as resilience against perturbations and adversarial attacks.
evidence.excerpt: Robustness15,25, as an extrinsic metric, explores the resilience of healthcare chatbots against perturbations and adversarial attacks.

evidence.claim: Bias evaluation is explicitly discussed for healthcare chatbots.
evidence.excerpt: Representation bias, occurring when certain groups or medical conditions are underrepresented or overlooked in the training data of the language model, leading to incomplete or inaccurate information.

evidence.claim: Authors discuss implementation challenges for metric definition.
evidence.excerpt: we engage in a discussion concerning the challenges associated with defining and implementing these metrics, with particular emphasis on confounding factors such as the target audience, evaluation methods, and prompt techniques
